The release carries exactly that: ARVideoFormat's own instance list in ARKitCore of the arm64e shared cache of iOS 16.0 is 28 twelve-byte entries and one of them is isVideoHDRSupported at 0x1af0f4870. The port answers NO (ARKit/ARVideoFormat.m), and NO is what the camera gives: HDR is a property of the pixel format a capture device offers, and every format this port builds an ARVideoFormat from is an AVCaptureDeviceFormat, which on the releases this package builds carries no HDR format at all. Controls of the read: the list resolves and prints all 28 selectors with their implementation addresses, so a read that found nothing would print nothing
entries.effect: NO, which is what a camera whose formats carry no HDR answers; the port's answer and the camera's are the same statement

entries.reason: carried: the recommendation is chosen out of the formats the camera really has, by the log-distance of each format's two dimensions from 3840x2160, so a format offered here is one the session can be configured with and the nearest one is the nearest the camera's own list allows. The input is +supportedVideoFormats, which reads CharonARTracker's own list of the back camera's formats, so the recommendation cannot name a format the camera does not have; when no format is close the answer is nil, which is what the property's own nullability says. The release carries the class method at 0x1af0f2a14
entries.effect: the offered format whose frame is closest to 3840x2160 on the log of each dimension, or nil when the camera offers none that is close
